header:
Date: 2025-02-12 | Time: 16:00 PT | Duration: 62m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Iris Valdez (Redwood), Dr. Lina Ortega (Synapse), Rahul Menon (Synapse CTO), Tom Alvarez (Synapse NLP), Sara Kim (Synapse Sec), Marta Ruiz (PM)
summary: POC scoping for model selection focused on open-model shortlist, tradeoffs for multilingual radiology notes, benchmark plan and 4-week timeline. Key asks: sample data, benchmark runs (hosted vs dedicated), security docs, and final success criteria weights.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone thanks for making time today, we'll keep this tight 60 minutes and scope the POC for model selection.
[00:08] Dr. Lina Ortega: Thanks, we want to validate a few open models for clinical note summarization and triage — importantly Spanish and Portuguese support as well as protected health info handling.
[00:18] Marcus Patel: Got it. Quick intro from our side — Marcus, SE, I'll drive the bench config. Are there any hard latency SLOs you need?
[00:25] Rahul Menon: Latency ideally p95 under 500ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens) for our triage flow; batch async is okay for bulk summarization. Cost target is also pretty important — if we can get near current OP costs that's a win.
[00:38] Tom Alvarez: Also note context length: our transcripts go up to 4k tokens occasionally, sometimes 8k for full reports.
[00:46] Sara Kim: Security requirements: HIPAA bound, SOC2 compliance, audit logs, SAML SSO, KMS for keys, and network peering (V P C peering) if we do private.
[00:58] Avery Chen: Thanks. High level POC plan we recommend: week 0 - onboarding & data handoff, week 1 - baseline runs on 3 models hosted, week 2 - dedicated GPU runs with quantized variants, week 3 - evals + regression checks, week 4 - decision and pricing. That roughly map to what you had in mind?
[01:12] Marta Ruiz: Yes, that looks fine. Curious on which models you suggest we start with — we prefer open models for cost and control but need quality for medical text.
[01:20] Marcus Patel: Our short list we usually try: Llama2-13B (2q/4q), Mistral Large 7B or 8B, MPT-30B in trimmed form, and a tuned Vicuna 13B variant. We'll run both base FP16 and int8/4-bit quantized configs to see quality dropoff.
[01:36] Dr. Lina Ortega: Any concerns about hallucination in these open models? We need high factuality for patient notes.
[01:42] Marcus Patel: Hallucination risk increases with quantization and smaller models. That's why we'll run targeted evals: entity-level F1 for key PHI redaction, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization and a domain rubric we can share. We also do safety filters and grounding with retrieval if needed.
[01:58] Tom Alvarez: Grounding is interesting. We have a de-id knowledge base we could use. Is the retrieval piece part of the POC or out of scope?
[02:05] Avery Chen: We can include a minimal retrieval baseline — vector store + top-k context — to test grounded responses. But keep it optional; first pass is pure generation quality.
[02:13] Rahul Menon: On throughput: ballpark expected concurrent requests? Right now near 120 qps peak, but only ~30 concurrent synchronous triage calls. Bulk workloads are nightly jobs.
[02:22] Marcus Patel: For sizing we'll provision a dedicated pool for peak concurrency and a hosted path for burst. For example, 3 x A100-equivalent for dedicated can sustain approx 30 concurrent streams on 13B depending on sequence length; we'll model p50/p95.
[02:36] Sara Kim: If we do dedicated, we need network diagrams and the KMS flow. Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[02:42] Avery Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS; we'll include integration notes. We'll also provide SOC2 docs and a red-team summary.
[02:50] Dr. Lina Ortega: For multilingual — Spanish is critical, Portuguese next priority, English obviously. How do these models compare?
[02:57] Marcus Patel: Mistral and MPT have decent multilingual transfer but Llama2 derivatives with fine-tuning often perform best. We'll include a small in-domain fine-tune or instruction-tune run in week 2 to test lift. Vicuna variants often handle instruction style prompts better but may need domain tuning.
[03:12] Tom Alvarez: Do you recommend starting with instruction-tuned checkpoints or base then tune?
[03:17] Marcus Patel: Start with instruction-tuned to get conversational quality, then run a small domain-tune on sampled notes (few-shot + LoRA depending on time). For POC speed, LoRA is fastest.
[03:26] Martina (muffled - speaker not clear): [crosstalk] question on eval metrics — can you share the rubric?
[03:30] Avery Chen: Yes we'll share 'POC-eval-rubric.md' — primary metric will be domain QA pass rate (entities, critical findings), secondary metrics are ROUGE-L and human preference tests on 200 examples.
[03:41] Rahul Menon: Timeline: we need decision by early March to budget for Q2. Can this POC finish with actionable results by 2025-03-07?
[03:48] Marcus Patel: Yes that's tight but doable with parallel hosted and dedicated runs. We'll need the sample dataset by 2025-02-18 to hit those dates.
[03:56] Sara Kim: For legal/procurement: what about data residency and logs — do you keep request logs in hosted mode? Are they redact-able?
[04:03] Avery Chen: Hosted stores logs for 30 days by default and we can configure retention; we also offer suppression and on-request deletion for PII if needed. For Private you'll keep logs in your VPC. We'll include logging configs in the security pack.
[04:13] Tom Alvarez: Benchmark specifics — what exact tests will you run?
[04:17] Marcus Patel: We'll run: latency p50/p95 for 3 prompt lengths (short 64, med 512, long 2k), throughput (tokens/sec) for batch of 8/32, quality evals on 500 dev examples, entity F1 for PHI redaction, and a hallucination checklist. We'll include both FP16 and int8/4-bit quantized runs.
[04:34] Marta Ruiz: Cost modeling — can Redwood give per-token and per-hour estimates for hosted vs dedicated so we can compare total cost for projected volume?
[04:40] Avery Chen: Yes — Marcus will generate a cost model spreadsheet showing projected monthly costs across volumes and quant levels. We'll present incremental cost reductions for caching/prefix caching benefits.
[04:51] Dr. Lina Ortega: On caching — can you cache patient prefixes or is that a privacy no-no?
[04:55] Sara Kim: That depends — we can't cache PHI unless it's encrypted and access-controlled; de-id first.
[05:01] Marcus Patel: For the POC we'll simulate prefix caching with de-identified contexts to measure performance gains but production design will respect your compliance rules.
[05:10] Tom Alvarez: About model selection — can you include any examples where a 7B Mistral beat a 13B Llama2 in our domain?
[05:17] Marcus Patel: Anecdotally yes on some instruction tasks, smaller models with better tokenization or instruction tuning can outperform bigger ones for latency-sensitive tasks. We'll include a few contrastive samples in the bench report. But expect quality tradeoffs on long-context summarization.
[05:29] Marta Ruiz: For success criteria we said weights earlier — can we lock that now?
[05:33] Avery Chen: Proposed: Quality 60% (human + entity F1), p95 latency 25% (must be below your cutoff), cost 15% (projected monthly). We'll mark thresholds in the rubric doc.
[05:43] Rahul Menon: If a hosted model meets quality but fails cost, we'd consider dedicated or quantization. If quality is insufficient we may look at retrieval augmentation.
[05:51] Marcus Patel: Exactly, we'll surface both spectrum options and an automated fallback policy suggestion: try hosted L2 for correctness then fallback to a cheaper smaller model for non-critical summaries.
[06:00] Dr. Lina Ortega: Any blockers on our side?
[06:04] Tom Alvarez: We'll need to confirm exportability of sample notes and a dev S3. Also legal sign-off for PHI de-id.
[06:10] Avery Chen: Perfect. We'll also share a minimal test harness and an example benchmark script run command.
[06:15] Sara Kim: Please include the network diagram and an example VPC peering flow; also note any ports we need to open for benching.
[06:22] Avery Chen: Noted — security pack will include network diagram.drawio and KMS flow.
[06:26] Marcus Patel: One more thing — quantization tooling we use will be specified; some 4-bit paths need specific CUDA kernels or A100-optimized runtimes; we'll call that out so you know hardware needs.
[06:38] Dr. Lina Ortega: Great. Last question — multilingual eval: will you run native speakers or automated metrics?
[06:44] Marcus Patel: We'll do both: automated metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore where applicable) plus human review for 100 Spanish and 50 Portuguese samples. We'll include inter-annotator agreement.
[06:54] Avery Chen: Ok let's recap next steps: we'll share the spreadsheet and bench harness by Friday, Synapse provides data by Tue, Marcus builds configs, security gets docs to Sara, and we reconvene first week of March for results.
[07:05] Rahul Menon: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:08] Marta Ruiz: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:10] [meeting ends]
